subject: zombie
label: zombie, in the place of the game's models/zombie.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/scientist.mdl, models/hassassin.mdl, models/gman.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, B, D, D where the asset was B, D, D, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words, the outline reads as a hunched, shambling walker: the left and front-left views show the head and arms carried forward and the back bent, the coat hanging off a stooped frame, and the back view matches. Nothing sticks out or is missing in any view.

M2.reason: Measured height is 67.5 against the brief's 68 (0.7% off), well inside 15%. Width 32 and depth 27.3 are not set by the brief, so they are not charged.

M3.reason: The coat, its torn hem, and the blood on the chest, shoulder and back are all there. The long clawed hands are weak: each hand carries only a few short white shards (front view at the lower right, left view at the sleeve ends) that read as small spikes, not long claws. The parasite over the head reads as a tan, lumpy bald head with dark eye sockets and a white ridge, not a separate body draped over the head.

M4.reason: Against the brief: a white coat, dark trousers and shoes, tan skin on the head, and dark red blood on the chest, back and shoulder, with dark bloodied hands. The materials read as the brief asks, and the regions agree from view to view.

M5.reason: Surface detail matches the brief: jagged tears along the coat's hem and sleeves, dark streaks and wounds on the face and head, and the blood smear on the chest and back. These are in their places and sharp enough at the size the game shows.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, which is measured apart: the asset was taken for one of the game's in 3 of 4 readings (picked C, B, D, D where it stood at B, D, D, B). The cap holds it at 2 here.

M7.reason: The front faces the front view, the figure stands upright on its feet at the origin, and the floor line in the walk frames sits under both feet.

M8.reason: 658 triangles is under twice the median of Half-Life's own creatures of its kind (2 x 504 = 1008), and under the third quartile (731). The harness reports no check errors. The views show no open or inside-out faces; the underside is closed as far as a player can see.

C1.reason: In the walk frames (0 to 23) the legs alternate, the arms swing with the body, and the head and coat stay attached, with nothing floating or sinking. In the attack frames (0 to 7) the claw shards follow the hands through the swing and stay with them, though they are small enough that they could be seen to drift slightly at this resolution.
